## [0.11.0] - 2026-07-29

The **HTTP/2 release**. The engine's code has set `CURL_HTTP_VERSION_2TLS` and enabled `CURLPIPE_MULTIPLEX` for a while, but the linked libcurl never actually had HTTP/2 in it - vcpkg's default `curl` port ships without nghttp2 - so every request, on both Send and load test, ran HTTP/1.1 regardless of what was asked for. This release links nghttp2 for real and adds a way to choose the protocol, so the engine half is genuinely new C++ (the vcpkg link, a `HttpVersion` domain type, the curl mapping) and the app half is a new control that reaches the whole execution path (Settings tab, MCP tool schemas, run history, the raw response view).

### Added

- **Real HTTP/2 negotiation**, on both Send and load test. The engine's `curl` dependency now requests the `http2` feature (pulling in nghttp2), so the `CURL_HTTP_VERSION_2TLS` the engine was already setting finally does something.
- **One Protocol control**, in the request builder's **Settings** tab, governing Send and load test alike - there is no separate load-test-only picker. `Auto` lets ALPN negotiate (curl's own default); `HTTP/1.1` forces it; `HTTP/2` attempts h2 over TLS and falls back to 1.1 over plain `http://` (curl's own `2TLS` semantics - silent by design, since a URL is often an unresolved `{{variable}}` at write time).
- **A Default HTTP Version setting** seeds the protocol a newly created request starts with. It's a write-time default only: changing it later never alters a request that's already saved, which matters for a load-testing tool where a global toggle silently changing every saved request's protocol would invalidate comparisons against historical runs.
- **The response's Raw tab shows the protocol that was actually negotiated**, instead of the hardcoded `HTTP/1.1` it printed before no matter what ran.
- **Run history and a run's final report show the protocol that was requested.** A load run makes many exchanges and so has no single negotiated protocol to report, so the sidebar row and the report's config row show the setting the run asked for - which is the value that is meaningful when comparing two runs.
- **MCP's `run_request` and `start_load_run` tools** accept the same `httpVersion` choice, so an agent can ask for HTTP/2 the same way the app does.

### Changed

- **Settings entries can now be a labelled picker, not just a number or a toggle.** A new `enum` config type (with an `options` column of `{value, label}` pairs) backs the Default HTTP Version setting and is available to any future picker-style setting - previously the settings UI only knew how to render `integer` and `boolean`.
- **A run's redirect policy is now reported by the API.** `followRedirects` / `maxRedirects` have been stored on every run since 0.10.0 but never left the database; they now ride along with the new `httpVersion` field into both `GET /runs`'s compact summary and a run's final report. No screen displays them yet - this makes them available to anything reading the API.

### Internal

`docs/architecture.md` claimed the engine's libcurl gave "HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3" - wrong before this release (HTTP/2 wasn't linked) and still wrong after it (HTTP/3 is an explicit non-goal: it needs ngtcp2 + nghttp3 and pins the TLS backend to OpenSSL). Corrected, along with a full pass over the engine API reference, DB schema, and MCP docs for the new field.
